classification.habit: Perennial rhizomatous herb 2–4 m with leafy pseudostems; panicles arise from base
classification.habitat: Moist, shaded evergreen forests at about 600–1500 m; grown as a shade-loving plantation crop.
classification.distribution: Native to the Western Ghats; cultivated mainly in Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

identification.description: Small aromatic greenish-yellow capsules containing numerous dark angular seeds.
identification.whole_plant: Tall perennial herb (2–4 m) with a thick underground rhizome and erect leafy pseudostems formed by overlapping leaf sheaths.
identification.root: Thick, fleshy, branched rhizome bearing fibrous roots; not a used part.
identification.stem: Aerial "stem" is a pseudostem of sheathing leaf bases; the true stem is the creeping rhizome.
identification.leaf: Distichous, lanceolate leaves 30–90 cm long with sheathing bases and a short ligule, dark green above and paler beneath.
identification.flower: Flowers on long panicles arising from the base of the pseudostem near the ground; corolla pale greenish-white with a white labellum streaked violet or pink.
identification.fruit: Fruit 1–2 cm long, ovoid or oblong, more or less three-sided with rounded angles, greenish to pale buff, shortly beaked, trilocular, each containing about 15–20 seeds adhering in a compact mass.
identification.seed: Seed dark brown to black, about 4 mm long, irregularly angular, transversely wrinkled, with a longitudinal channel for the raphe and a thin membranous aril; strongly aromatic.
identification_points: Dark brown angular, transversely wrinkled seeds in compact masses
Seeds enclosed in a thin colourless aril
Panicles arise from the base of the leafy pseudostem

therapeutics.precautions: Generally well tolerated in culinary and pharmacopoeial doses; use whole, well-stored capsules as the volatile oil is lost from exposed powder. Large amounts may irritate in hyperacidity.
therapeutics.contraindications: Known hypersensitivity. Use cautiously in gallstone colic, where aromatic spice therapy is conventionally avoided.

shlokas:
सूक्ष्मोपकुञ्चिका तुत्था कोरङ्गी द्राविडी त्रुटिः ।
एला सूक्ष्मा कफश्वासकासार्शोमूत्रकृच्छ्रहृत् ।
रसे तु कटुका शीता लघ्वी वातहरी मता ॥६३॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The seeds owe their aroma to an essential oil dominated by 1,8-cineole and α-terpinyl acetate, which is lost on prolonged storage of powdered seed.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Improves digestion, relieves nausea and freshens breath.
recognized_uses: Flavouring corrigent in many formulations, e.g. Sitopaladi Churna
modern_information.safety_notes: Regarded as safe in food amounts; occasional contact allergy is reported. Medicinal use should follow pharmacopoeial doses.

exam_points: Botanical name: Elettaria cardamomum (Sukshma Ela); Family: Zingiberaceae
Useful part: seeds and dried fruit capsule
Rasa: Katu-Madhura; Guna: Laghu-Ruksha; Virya: Sheeta; Vipaka: Madhura
Key karma: Chhardighna, Mukhashodhaka, Mutrala, Deepana
Differentiate from Brihat Ela (Amomum subulatum, large cardamom)
Formulations: Eladi Churna, Eladi Modaka, Sitopaladi Churna (API)

doctor.quick_reference: Sukshma Ela is a Sheeta, Madhura-vipaka aromatic used for Chhardi, Aruchi, Mukhadurgandhya, Kasa-Shwasa and Mutrakrichhra; seed churna 250–500 mg.
key_precautions: Use fresh whole capsules for potency
Caution in hyperacidity with large amounts
